title: Incorrect Material Display
body: ### Tested versions v4.6.dev4.official [bd2ca13c6] v4.6.dev3.official [9d84f3d13] v4.6.dev2.official [7864ac8] v4.6.dev1.official [8d8041b] v4.5.stable.official [876b290], v4.5.beta6.official [d5ad055], v4.5.beta5.official [c81fd6c], v4.5.beta4.official [2d113cc], v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7] ### Issue description I decided to make things a bit easier for whoever will work on this issue. I initially described it in #109332, but that report contained three related problems together (incorrect display of materials/models/textures — since these are interconnected). Therefore, I think it’s time to finally split it up for clarity, especially after fix #112046, which resolves part of the issue starting from 4.6.dev3. (Yes, I couldn’t find a way to make that one a parent issue — it would be great if that could be done. Then I could, for example, link the remaining two, and once all three are resolved, we could close everything neatly. Please share your thoughts on this below. But at least separating this specific material-related problem is worth doing right now.) (Also, AThousandShips, please — I hope you won’t nitpick this one, same as others did. The system here doesn’t play any role, unlike in the original issue, so I’ll omit it for simplicity, along with the MRP. But you can verify this bug the same way the contributor did in #109332, or as others who already confirmed the issue. However, if you still insist on formality or have concerns, please say so too.) ### Steps to reproduce So, to make things clearer, here are some examples: This is a .glb wardrobe model exported from Blender and placed into a Godot scene. We can see a white material sphere (visually incorrect display), even though it actually renders correctly on the model itself. It can appear checkered (#112046 fixes this), white, or transparent. The issue can currently be avoided by making the material unique. However, that’s a poor workaround — because the issue isn’t caused by material uniqueness, and even a normal model can display incorrectly for no reason (that’s why I’m showing it within a scene, because even there it behaves incorrectly — not to mention imported .glb models). Here’s another object, for example. It looks like it simply doesn’t refresh the display, but when it does, we might face another issue. In #109332, this visual effect was described in the context of scene preview rendering. In short, we can observe a similar effect on the material sphere — instead of showing the current material, it displays the one from the previous model. I also have a question about fix #112046 — does it address the effect shown below? Because that wasn’t mentioned in the resolution details: In theory, this should relate to the same issue, but if you prefer, we can move it into a separate one (since it’s in the GUI — maybe it’s something different, etc.). However, from what I can see, the same problems described above appear repeatedly in the tree view (duplication, white sphere, checkered sphere — though I haven’t seen a transparent one here, but it does appear sometimes when viewing materials).
